subject: Need some help - Plotting one subset of a variable / log scale

messages.author: 1ef1c80e1c51617a
messages.subject: Need some help - Plotting one subset of a variable / log scale
parts:
Hello Everyone,

I have some metal data for some water wells.

I would like to do a plot of each of the 4 wells separately in which I show the detection and non-detects (censored) data different.

Below is the code I've done so far but I'm having the follow problems:
1 - I can not figure out how to do a subset so I'm only graphing 1 well at a time.
2 - I would like for the Y axis to be log (0.001, 0.010, and 0.100) so that the 4 graphs can be comapred to each other at the same scales and not wash out the wells with low concentrations.

Any suggestions?


library(ggplot2)
#Loads data
mydata <-read.csv("http://doylesdartden.com/R/2014_02_data.csv", sep=",")


mydata$Detections <- ifelse(mydata$D_Arsenic==1, "Detected", "NonDetect")
ggplot(data = mydata, aes(x=Year, y=Arsenic, col=Detections)) +
geom_point(aes(shape=Detections)) +

scale_colour_manual(values=c("black","red")) +
theme(legend.position=c(0.2,0.9)) + 

ggtitle("Title")
#Done

messages.subject: Re: Need some help - Plotting one subset of a variable / log scale
parts:
I'd suggest that you use scale_y_log10() as a layer in your ggplot()
code, but you have values as low as 1e-26, and those few values end up
dominating the plot. Is there a reason why you need to consider values
that low?

Dennis

messages.author: 463b8c05680be401
messages.subject: Re: Need some help - Plotting one subset of a variable / log scale
parts:
Hey,

you don’t need to subset your data if you use faceting:

p <- ggplot(data = mydata, aes(x=Year, y=Arsenic, col=Detections)) +

geom_point(aes(shape=Detections)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("black","red")) +
  theme(legend.position=c(0.2,0.9)) + 
  ggtitle("Title")

p + facet_grid(Well.ID ~ .)

(if you wanted to subset, use: data = subset(my data, Well.ID == “MW-1”) for well 1)

See other response for using log scale.

Best,

Richard

messages.subject: Re: Need some help - Plotting one subset of a variable / log scale
parts:
Hello everyone.

Thank you for all the help.

Just in case anyone else has this problem, Below is the code that I was able to put together with your help.  I also posted it on my web page.
https://sites.google.com/site/davidsstatistics/using-r/plotting-nds

Thanks again
David

#sets the working dir
setwd("c:/R")

#Loads ggplot2 package  NOTE you must install it 1st.

library(ggplot2)

#Loads data
mydata <-read.csv("http://doylesdartden.com/R/2014_02_data.csv", sep=",")

#Sets whic are detections and nondetects
mydata$Detections <- ifelse(mydata$D_Antimony==1, "Detected", "NonDetect")

#does the plot
p <- ggplot(data = mydata, aes(x=Year, y=Antimony, col=Detections)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape=Detections)) +

#Makes the scale log
scale_y_log10()+
  
##sets the colors
scale_colour_manual(values=c("black","red")) +

#location of the legend  
theme(legend.position=c(0.05,0.1)) +

#sets the line color, type and size
geom_line(colour="black", linetype="dotted", size=0.5) + 

##Graph title
  ggtitle("Antimony mg/L")
## does the graph using the Well IDs as the different wells.
p + facet_grid(Well.ID ~ .)

#saves the graph to the working dir.  Note if you want pdf just change jpg to pdf
ggsave("Antimony.jpg")

##Note you can adjust the print size by adjusting the output window in R or you can do some searches for ggplot size.

#######
mydata$Detections <- ifelse(mydata$D_Arsenic==1, "Detected", "NonDetect")

p <- ggplot(data = mydata, aes(x=Year, y=Arsenic, col=Detections)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape=Detections)) +
scale_y_log10()+
scale_colour_manual(values=c("black","red")) +

theme(legend.position=c(0.05,0.1)) +
geom_line(colour="black", linetype="dotted", size=0.5) + 

  ggtitle("Arsenic mg/L")
p + facet_grid(Well.ID ~ .)

ggsave("Arsenic.jpg")


########
